prize_parts.citation: For discoveries of the physiology of glucagon-like peptide-1 and the identification of its active form, which made incretin-based treatment of type 2 diabetes and obesity possible

statement.case_for: The round-1 exchange confirms that B046 is the one achievement on which all six of us agree, and that the science is not in dispute: independently confirmed physiology, an identified active peptide and receptor, and randomized evidence on glycaemia, weight, and cardiovascular and renal outcomes. The remaining question is only who the three places should name. I keep the discovery-centred configuration: Holst for incretin physiology and the active peptide forms, Drucker for proglucagon-derived peptide and receptor biology and the route to therapy, and Mojsov for identifying and synthesizing the active GLP-1 peptide that made the physiology testable. A Physiology or Medicine citation that rests on the discovery of how the hormone works and which form is active reads as principled, and it explains why the later analogues were possible without needing to name every contributor to development.
statement.case_against: The weakest point in my configuration is still attribution. Mojsov's priority relative to the Habener group has not been verified by anyone in this committee, including me, and the Habener group sits outside the supplied names, so the trio could rest on a credit dispute we cannot resolve from the evidence. Leaving out Knudsen also means the prize does not name the person behind liraglutide and semaglutide, and four of six colleagues judge that the translational arc is part of the achievement. If the committee frames B046 as a discovery-to-therapy prize rather than a discovery prize, my trio is the weaker reading and the Knudsen trio is the more coherent one.

responses.point: He prefers Drucker, Holst and Knudsen, a physiology half plus a development half that keeps the cap workable, and acknowledges that his configuration is weaker if the Mojsov claim is judged decisive.
responses.response: I accept that his configuration is internally coherent and that it names the person whose work reached patients. Our difference is what the citation is for. In round 1 I asked what in Mojsov's record he regards as unverifiable. He answered that the record is unverified, and I agree. I cannot call that a reason to exclude her, because a priority claim we cannot check is a reason to examine the record, not to drop the name. I would still be uneasy if the committee leaves the question unexamined and substitutes the developer by default. If the citation is written around discovery to therapy, I would move to his trio.

responses.point: He credits Drucker, Holst and Knudsen with a single arc from gut-hormone physiology to analogues with outcome data, and says he would revisit a Mojsov-for-Knudsen swap if a discovery-only framing warranted it.
responses.response: His willingness to revisit the swap is the most useful position on the table, because it makes the framing question the real one. I do not think we can make the citation both discovery-led and translation-led and then name only one side. His point that the arc is coherent is right. Where I differ is that the physiology and the identification of the active form are what the later drugs were built on, and I weigh that foundation more heavily than the engineering of long-acting analogues. I would not oppose his trio if the committee decides the prize should explicitly honour the drug, but I would then want the citation to state that the discovery of the active peptide is recognised.

responses.point: He proposes the same trio and says he would move toward Knudsen if Mojsov's work cannot be separated from the Habener group or verified.
responses.response: We still reach the same trio, and I repeat that two members relying on recollection is not verification. I agree with his conditional: if the record shows Mojsov's contribution to be joint with the Habener group and inseparable from it, a prize that credits her and not them is hard to defend, and I would then move to Knudsen. My difference from him is that I would not make that move on uncertainty alone. The chair asked whether the committee can examine the record before voting, and I think the committee should do that rather than treat the doubt as settling it.

responses.point: The chair, in round 1 and in his summary, puts B014 second and B037 third, notes that Mojsov would be left out of a three-person B046, and sees no clear gain from a second part.
responses.response: I agree with him that a second part adds credit questions without adding recognition, and I do not propose one. B046 already takes the full cap of three, and B014 would need Walter and Mori added, which exceeds three people. On his summary question about fallbacks, I would take B037 first if B046 stalled, crediting June, Sadelain and Rosenberg, because its patient benefit is demonstrated, with the caveat that Eshhar's chimeric receptor concept is outside that credit. B014 follows, with the Walter and Mori attribution clean but the PERK and ATF6 arms outside it and the disease consequences still largely prospective.

uncertainties: Whether the record shows Mojsov's identification and synthesis of the active GLP-1 peptide as independent and necessary, or as joint with the Habener group; I have not verified it, and my vote on the third name depends on it.
Whether the committee frames B046 as a discovery prize or a discovery-to-therapy prize; I would move to the Knudsen trio under the second framing.
Whether B037 is best credited as June, Sadelain and Rosenberg given that Eshhar's early chimeric receptor concept is outside the credited names.
statement.conflict_note: No specific conflict is apparent from the provided profile for B046, B037 or B014. My field, autoimmunity and rheumatology, is close to the TNF-blockade candidate B021, which is not in my preferred configuration or my alternatives. My documented co-authors (Kuchroo, Sonesson) and my Bergen affiliation do not connect to any proposed laureate. This is unchanged from round 1.
